title: Forgiveness
description: Fifteen minutes of forgiveness in three directions: asking for it, offering it, and forgiving yourself.

segments.say: Sit comfortably and let your eyes close.
Breathe slowly a few times. Feel the area of the chest, around the heart.
Forgiving is not saying that what happened was okay. And it is not forgetting.
It is putting down the weight of something that is already over. Before anything, it is a relief for the one who forgives.
And it cannot be forced. If forgiveness does not come today, that is fine. The intention is already a start.
We will practise in three directions.
First, asking for forgiveness.
Remember someone you hurt, on purpose or not. Out of fear, out of anger, out of carelessness.
Feel the pain you caused, without drowning in it.
Say silently: for the ways I have hurt you, I ask your forgiveness.
Now, the second direction. Offering forgiveness.
Remember someone who hurt you. Start with something small, not the deepest wound.
Notice the pain that is still there. And the weight of carrying it.
That person also acted out of their own pain, their own confusion.
Say silently: for the ways you have hurt me, I forgive you. As much as I can right now.
And now, the third direction. For many people, the hardest. Forgiving yourself.
Remember something you still hold against yourself. A mistake, a choice, something you did not do.
Look at who you were in that moment. What you knew, what you felt, what was possible.
Say silently: for the ways I have hurt myself, I forgive myself.
Notice what is left. Maybe lightness, maybe resistance, maybe both.
Forgiveness is a practice, not a moment. You can come back to it as often as you need.
May I forgive. May I be forgiven.
May I be at peace.
When you are ready, open your eyes.
